blurb:
Wilson came in from animal control, went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, landed in a foster home, and by all accounts has been an absolute joy the whole way through. He's three years old, about 46 pounds, Bulldog and Boxer mixed, and he runs on enthusiasm. Not anxious energy. Just pure, happy, this-is-the-best-day-of-my-life energy, every day.

He's a talker. Wilson narrates his playtime with vocalizations, his foster family calls it chatting, and his trainer actually uses him to help other dogs learn how to play because he's that good with them. He does great with dogs who don't mind a vocal playmate. He met kids of various ages at his foster home and handled it well, calm and affectionate. Just skip the toddler introductions since he's big enough to accidentally knock a small kid over.

No cats. He's got a prey drive toward small animals on walks, so that's a firm no. But if you've got a dog-friendly household, older kids, and you're looking for a dog who's going to make you laugh every single day, Wilson is worth a visit. He even drank from the sprayer during his bath and handed out kisses the whole time. That's the kind of dog he is.

Submit an inquiry at mostlymutts.org or stop by to meet him in person.

scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups training plus foster success plus kid-compatibility makes him a well-rounded, confidence-inspiring adoption for families
• The "chatty dog who teaches other dogs to play" detail is genuinely memorable and gives a newsletter feature a natural headline
• Animal control origin and program graduation suggest a moderate shelter timeline, but his energy and appeal likely keep the wait manageable

blurb:
Glynnis is eight years old, about 41 pounds, came in from animal control, went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, and has spent time in multiple foster homes. Every single person who has spent time with her says a version of the same thing. The volunteers called her super sweet and precious. Her foster family called her the sweetest dog ever. She melts into you for scratches. She gives kisses. When she sleeps, she dreams and makes little noises and kicks her feet around. That's who Glynnis is.

She does best in a quieter home with more space. An apartment with lots of foot traffic and other dogs passing in close quarters wasn't the right fit. A house where she can settle in and feel like she belongs? That's where she's going to shine. She's gentle, easy-going, and reportedly happy just to be near her people. She did fine meeting young kids at the shelter, so a home with children 10 and up should be no problem.

She'd do best as an only dog, and no cats. She tried to chase one in a foster home, so that one's pretty clear. But if you've got a calm household and you've been thinking about adding a dog who just wants to be your loyal, cuddly companion, go meet Glynnis. She's been waiting long enough.

Visit mostlymutts.org to submit an inquiry or find out more.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Multiple foster placements, senior age, and a quiet-home-only requirement make her statistically one of the hardest to place—newsletter exposure could be decisive
• Universal praise from every volunteer and foster who met her creates a credible, chorus-of-advocates narrative that builds reader trust
• "She's been waiting long enough" mirrors Bernadette's language but carries more weight given her age and multi-placement history—urgency is real and documented

blurb:
Eugene has already proven he can be somebody's whole world. He spent about a year with his person before they had to leave the country and couldn't take him along. His former owner was sad about it. That's not a throwaway detail. That's a dog who earned real love from someone and had it taken away through no fault of his own. Now he's back at Mostly Mutts, readjusting, and looking for round two.

He's about six years old, 17 pounds, and described by people who've spent time with him as a sweet lap dog. He doesn't want to play with toys. He wants to be next to you. Once he feels safe, that's exactly what he does. He's sensitive and takes time to warm up, especially with leashing and harnessing, so he needs a patient household that's willing to move at his pace. He did best as an only dog with his previous family, though he's open to meeting other dogs. He lived with a cat before and did fine.

Eugene would do best with adults or teens 15 and up who understand how to read a dog's body language and give him room to breathe. If you have a quiet home and some patience to spare, go meet him. Submit an inquiry or stop by Mostly Mutts to get started.

Mostly Mutts is located in Kennesaw.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• A dog returned through circumstance—not behavior—whose former owner grieved the separation is a rare, reader-stopping story
• Specific household requirements (adults/teens 15+, patient home, likely only dog) narrow the pool and signal he may wait longer without visibility
• Readjusting after a real bond was broken gives this feature genuine emotional urgency that drives reader action

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Named after the Scrubs character, which feels right. Elliot is four months old, about four pounds, and she came into Mostly Mutts as a young kitten who just needed a stable place to land. She got that, got healthy, and now she's ready to move somewhere permanent.

She plays hard with toys, collects cuddles from anyone willing, and keeps her litter box clean without any drama. She's already spayed, microchipped, and up to date on all her shots, so you're not walking into a vet bill situation on day one.

She gets along with other cats in her foster home, so pairing her with an existing cat isn't a problem. Dogs are unknown. She's good with gentle kids. If your house already has a cat who could use a playmate, Elliot would probably fit right in. Adoption fee is $175. She's in Kennesaw with Mostly Mutts. Reach out through their website or give them a call to set up a visit.
scoring_notes:
• Fully vetted kitten who plays, cuddles, and coexists with cats checks every box for a frictionless adoption
• Pop-culture name adds a light personality hook but the backstory offers little emotional depth for readers
• No urgency signals in the blurb suggest she's a recent intake unlikely to need newsletter intervention

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Four and a half months old, four and a half pounds, and already has more curiosity than most cats twice her age. Dory came in from animal control, landed in a good foster home, and has been absolutely thriving ever since.

She's a tabby mix with a lot going on. Explore everything, play hard, then find the nearest warm lap and stay there. That's her whole routine. She's litter trained, fully vaccinated, microchipped, and already spayed, so the hard part is done before she even gets home with you.

She does great with other cats, so if you've been on the fence about getting a second one, here's your opening. Dogs are unknown. Kids are welcome as long as they're gentle and know how to handle a small kitten. She's in Kennesaw with Mostly Mutts. Adoption fee is $175. Call, email, or submit an inquiry through their site to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Fully vetted, spayed, and kitten-aged makes her one of the lowest-friction adoptions in the batch
• Backstory is thin—animal control intake with no distinguishing narrative limits newsletter emotional pull
• Recent foster placement and thriving status suggest she arrived recently and won't wait long regardless

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
She started her life outside, had a litter of kittens at barely a year old, and somehow kept it together until a foster family found her in their backyard and brought the whole crew inside. Thats Bernadette. About one year old, seven and a half pounds, and somehow the most patient, gentle soul in the room despite everything she's been through.

Her kittens have mostly all moved on to their own homes now. Bernadette is next.

She's a little cautious when she first meets you. Not skittish, just careful. She's earned the right to take her time. But once she decides you're good people, she's going to press her head into your hand and not let you stop petting her. Her foster describes her as having a gentle soul with a lot of love to give, and from everything in her history, that tracks. She's litter trained, loves feather wands, and is happy to curl up beside you for hours once she's comfortable.

She's done great with the cats in her foster home, so she'd likely be fine with another calm cat at home. Dogs and kids are unknowns, but she's been sweet with the children she's met so far. Gentle kids would probably be fine. Mostly Mutts is based in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry through their website or call to get the process started. Bernadette has waited long enough.
scoring_notes:
• Young, gentle mama cat with a proven capacity for love makes her an emotionally resonant adoption candidate
• Stray-to-foster origin story with kittens adopted out before her creates a natural narrative hook for readers
• Phrase "Bernadette has waited long enough" signals she's been overlooked despite being ready—urgency is built in
